title: Focal genes: orthologue protein sequences across zebrafish, medaka, flying fish, bats, non-flying mammals, a flying insect and gliders
birds_excluded: Birds (class Aves) are this project's frozen holdout and are excluded until the holdout exam runs.
pterosaurs: Pterosaurs are extinct (Mesozoic) and have no DNA: no sequence comparison is possible; their only comparison is morphological (physics/flier/PRIOR-ART-FLIER.md).
flying_fish_status: Annotated Hirundichthys speculiger proteins exist (Xu et al. 2021, Front Genet 12:695700; figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.14600634.v1, pep.fa, 13 MB) for the same assembly as GCA_018398805.1 (which NCBI holds unannotated). Orthologues were called by reciprocal best blastp hit to the zebrafish proteome; where that fails (kcnh2a, shha) the alignment uses tblastn hits on the assembly, labelled. Medaka (Beloniformes) remains in every alignment as the closest Ensembl-annotated relative. H. speculiger is not one of the species measured for fin length by Daane 2021, so it is cross-species within the family.
drosophila_note: Drosophila orthologues exist in Ensembl for kcnk5b, kcnh2a, tbx5a and prdm1a only, all many-to-many or one-to-many and distant (26-52% identity); none for slc43a2a, gja1b (insects use innexins, not connexins), fgf10a, shha or hhip under these Ensembl calls. Insect wings are not homologous to vertebrate limbs or fins.
